themes.title: Slow down, pause and ban
themes.summary: A growing set of proposals would pause frontier development or prohibit superintelligence, usually paired with a call for an international treaty.
themes.direction: Rising in visibility, low odds of passage in the near term.

items.name: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (Sanders, Casar)
items.stance: Prohibit smarter-than-human AI; temporary pause on advanced AI development until safety rules exist; new federal agency.

items.name: Superintelligence ban bill (Alex Sobel MP)
items.status: Ten Minute Rule bill, first reading
items.stance: State powers to monitor and restrict precursors to superintelligence; pursue a global ban treaty. Drafted by campaign group ControlAI. Reported as the first such bill in any G7 parliament.

themes.title: Kill switches and shutdown powers
themes.summary: Proposals to require that powerful AI systems can be shut down, and to give the state the power to order it. Experts dispute how well this works in practice.
themes.direction: Gaining bipartisan traction in the US after a reported security incident; contested on feasibility.

items.name: AI Kill Switch Act (Lieu, Moran)
items.stance: Frontier models must have a kill switch; CISA sets coverage rules; DHS may order shutdown in emergencies including loss of control. Penalties reported up to $2m per day for missing the capability and $20m per day for ignoring a shutdown order.
items.note: Prompted by a reported security incident involving an autonomous AI agent during an internal evaluation; as described by Roll Call. Verify independently.

items.name: California executive order on AI safeguards (Newsom)
items.status: Executive order; agencies have about two months to recommend
items.stance: Recommend third-party audits of major labs and a kill switch. Not law. Newsom vetoed SB 1047 in 2024, which had a shutdown requirement.

themes.title: Federal preemption vs state action
themes.summary: The US federal government is pushing to override state AI laws while states keep legislating.
themes.direction: Contested. Congress has not passed preemption and leadership is sceptical.

items.name: Executive Order 14365 and the Great American AI Act draft
items.status: EO in force; bill is a discussion draft
items.stance: DOJ task force to challenge state laws; a draft bill would preempt state model-development rules for three years.
items.likelihood: Medium for litigation, low for statute

expert_views.view: A kill switch would be a set of lab-run protocols checked by independent bodies, not a literal button.
Newer models may resist shutdown; some researchers argue a kill switch cannot contain a superintelligent system and call for an international moratorium instead.
